impact_assessment.why: The first rewrite task closed with the schema-14 core, graph, evidence, cascades, reports, measurements, search and analysis ported; the remaining runtime-critical surface and outer layers still run only in Python.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every command the engine exposes will have a Rust implementation backed by the same SQLite graph, with parity tests before the Python entry point is retired.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: JSON/text shapes, manifest digests and bundle formats must match Python exactly; dependency: only declared crates and the shared graph; concurrency: other agents are editing AIKit's native gates, so project gates must be verified with direct scripts when the root native bridge is stale; state: existing research.db files must stay readable.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read each Python module before porting; add CLI-level parity scripts for every subsystem; keep new Rust modules pure and dependency-light; verify with cargo test plus direct hygiene/KB/secret/test scripts.

[1/6] Rust crate foundation: Cargo workspace, schema-14 SQLite store, frozen models/vocabularies, CLI skeleton

impact_assessment.why: User directive: full rewrite of research-engine in Rust; the Python core is ~10k lines and the whole tree ~79k lines, so the rewrite must be incremental, verifiable and keep the persistent contract.
impact_assessment.benefits: A compilable Rust core with schema-14 DB compatibility and CLI parity from milestone 1; each later milestone ports a bounded subsystem with golden tests against the Python engine.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: SQLite schema v14, ID formats, CLI flags and JSON shapes must stay byte-compatible; dependency: rusqlite/clap/serde must be declared and locked; concurrency: no other agent may write the project ledger; state: existing research.db files must remain readable and untouched.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read each Python module before porting; keep rusqlite bundled and pinned via Cargo.lock; own the ledger as opencode:rust-rewrite; open existing DBs read-only in golden tests and write only to temp copies.
